daily.summary: New initiative to promote research, innovation and industry-academia collaboration Hyderabad: Prof V Balakista Reddy, Chairman, Telangana Council of Higher Education (TGCHE), announced the launch of the Higher Education Research & Innovation Foundation (HERIF), a dedicated Section 8 not-for-profit company, aimed at mobilising alternative sources of funding to strengthen public universities in Telangana. Addressing the media on Wednesday, he said that through HERIF, universities can explore diverse resource-mobilisation opportunities, including Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) contributions, industry-sponsored research, consultancy services, corporate training, executive education, alum contributions, philanthropic donations, institutional endowments, and national and international research grants.

daily.title: Fast-Track Merger vs NCLT Route In 2026: Which Should Companies Choose?

Before a merger scheme can take effect, someone has to approve it. For most companies that someone is the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) , acting under Sections 230–232 of the Companies Act, 2013. Section 233 offers a shortcut for eligible companies: approval from the Regional Director (RD) of the Ministry of Corporate Affairs. The tribunal route is judicial and detailed.

daily.title: Importer Need Not Challenge Assessment For Refund After Anti-Dumping Duty Set At Nil: Bombay High Court
daily.summary: The Bombay High Court has held that an importer need not challenge the assessment of bills of entry to claim a refund of provisional anti-dumping duty when the final duty is determined as nil.“The... “The refund becomes automatic after the Second Notification is issued under Section 9A(1) of the Customs Tariff Act, 1975, and the same was required to be processed since the Anti-Dumping Duty was finally determined as 'Nil'. There is no necessity for the Respondent to thereafter file an appeal against the assessment or reassessment,” a bench of Justice B.P. Colabawalla and Justice Farhan P. Dubash observed.

daily.title: 47th Half-Yearly Report on Management of Foreign Exchange Reserves: April – September 2026
daily.summary: It may be recalled that in February 2004 , the Reserve Bank initiated the practice of compiling half-yearly reports on the management of foreign exchange reserves and making them public to promote greater transparency and enhance disclosure in the management of the country’s foreign exchange reserves. In this connection, Reserve Bank of India has today released the 47th Half-Yearly Report on Management of Foreign Exchange Reserves with reference to end-September 2026. During April-September 2026, India’s foreign exchange reserves increased from US$ 691.11 billion to US$ 737.78 billion.

breaking.title: SEBI may ease SIF norms further, consider giving fund managers more flexibility
breaking.summary: At Moneycontrol FiDEX 2.0, SEBI Executive Director Manoj Kumar says regulator is encouraged by the category's growth; specific changes are still under discussion. Market regulator Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) may further liberalise the regulatory framework for specialised investment funds (SIFs), with a view to giving fund managers greater flexibility to deploy investment strategies, Executive Director Manoj Kumar said in Mumbai. Kumar, however, did not specify the proposed changes, saying several matters were still under discussion. His remarks come amid industry demands for greater flexibility in deploying long-short strategies through SIFs, including higher gross exposure limits.

breaking.summary: Summary : The Reserve Bank of India’s draft Fifth Amendment Directions, 2026 propose new safeguards against fraudulent electronic banking transactions at Regional Rural Banks (RRBs). The draft builds on the June 2026 Third Amendment Directions and the April 2026 discussion paper on digital payment fraud safeguards . Most provisions would take effect on 1 July 2027, or earlier if an RRB chooses. Clauses (i) to (iv), (vii) and (viii) of the proposed definition of bank negligence would take effect on 1 January 2027.

breaking.title: Finance Ministry restricts media entry till Budget announcement
breaking.summary: The Finance Ministry has restricted media entry into Kartavya Bhavan-1 until the Union Budget presentation by Nirmala Sitharaman on February 1. According to sources, media personnel will be permitted to enter the building during this period only with specific approval from designated authorised officers. Officials concerned have also been directed to ensure strict compliance with the restrictions. The Union Budget for 2027-28 is scheduled to be presented on February 1. It will be the fourth Budget of the Modi 3.0 government and the 10th consecutive Budget presented by Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman, marking a rare milestone in the Parliamentary history.

breaking.title: Daily Voice: RBI unlikely to hike rates by more than 100 bps in current cycle, says Sushant Bhansali
breaking.summary: According to Sushant Bhansali of Ambit Asset Management, the earnings growth trajectory of Indian corporates is unlikely to be meaningfully impacted, given his expectation of only moderate rate hikes during this cycle. Sushant Bhansali, CEO of Ambit Asset Management, expects the RBI to raise interest rates by no more than 100 basis points in the current cycle, as non-food inflation is primarily linked to crude oil prices, which appear to be under control. Among sectors, he believes banks are attractively valued, supported by a healthy credit growth trajectory and the potential for net interest margin (NIM) expansion.
